messages.author: c30f454051765351
messages.subject: Error in igraph::topo_sort
parts:
Hi folks 
I am wondering if anyone here might be able to help me make sense of this error and the warning message. I'm not sure if they are linked. I am starting from a simpler open SCR model, which ran fine, and am now building in more temporal variability and individual variability in some terms when I ran in to this. I've never seen this error before and I'm not sure where to start with sorting it out. I can provide a dataset to replicate if that'd help. 

My hunch is that it has something to do with the trap matrix. The number of sites surveyed increased incrementally over the 7 year study period. In my earlier test runs I hadnt realized that the ntraps in model constants and the individual capture-history array was limited to the number of sites with detections rather than the total number of sites across years. After fixing this mistake I ran into this.  Thanks as always

fmod1 <- nimbleModel(code = fish_cjs, constants = m.const, inits = inits) Defining model [Note] Using 'Sex,y' (given within 'constants') as data. Error in igraph::topo_sort(graph, mode = "out") : At vendor/cigraph/src/properties/dag.c:125 : The graph has cycles; topological sorting is only possible in acyclic graphs. Invalid value In addition: Warning message: In cbind(edgesFrom, edgesTo) : number of rows of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 2)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error in igraph::topo_sort
parts:
Hi Ben,
Focusing on the error about cycles: This would mean that there is a chain of dependencies such that a node eventually depends on itself. This could be hard to track down if doing so depends on nested indexing. You mentioned temporal variability. If you have states changing through time, it is easy to have a mistake where the "t" vs "t-1" (and/or "t+1") are not all right and that can result in a cycle. Does that help?
Perry
